review_notes:
I read all 172 lines of the target file. I also read the definitions it depends on, `cavitySpectralImage` (CavitySpectralImages.lean) and `cavityNormalizeFrame` (CavityFrameAlgebra.lean), and grepped for downstream uses of the lemmas in this file: `cavitySpectralProjectors_sum` is used in CavityRetainedStack and CavityConcreteComplement, and `cavitySpectralSupport_eigen` is used in CavityBaseSpectralSum. Neither downstream use calls `simp` on these declarations. Other files in the same directory do add `@[simp]` `_apply` lemmas for their local matrix-valued definitions, for example `cavityColumnEquiv_apply` and `cavitySelectedGroupProjection_apply`.

The one clear simp-interface gap is `cavityGroupLift`. It has no evaluation lemma for the case `g i = a`. Its zero-case lemma exists but is not tagged simp and is never used inside the file's proofs. So every entry-wise proof unfolds the definition directly.

Things I considered and rejected:
- Making `cavityGroupLift_restrict` or `cavityGroupLift_gram` simp lemmas. `_restrict` has a support hypothesis that does not suit simp, and `_gram` is only ever used with `rw`.
- `cavitySpectralProjectors_sum` is used only by `rw`/`exact`, so a simp tag would not help those uses.
- `cavitySpectralImage` also lacks apply lemmas (line 58 unfolds it), but it is defined in another file, so I only mention it here.

I found no rewrite cycles or competing rules. I could not run Lean, so I have not checked the proposed lemmas or the shortened proofs by compiling them.

findings.problem: `cavityGroupLift` is a matrix built from a lambda with a dependent `if`. It has no canonical entry-wise simp lemmas. The zero case is stated as `cavityGroupLift_support`, but it is not tagged `@[simp]`, and none of the later proofs use it. There is no lemma at all for the case `g i = a`. As a result, each entry-wise proof unfolds the definition and reduces the `dite` by hand. The pattern `simp only [cavityGroupLift, hi, dite_true/dite_false, ...]` appears at lines 21, 36, 39, 48, 49, 88, 92, 96 and 99. This exposes the raw `if hi : g i = a then ... else 0` term in every goal. Each call has to bring in the case hypothesis and the right `dite_*` lemma, and the body stays coupled to the exact lambda/`dite` form of the definition.
findings.proposed_change:
Add two evaluation lemmas right after the definition and use them instead of unfolding:
```lean
@[simp] lemma cavityGroupLift_apply_of_eq {r m q t : ℕ} (g : Fin r → Fin m) (a : Fin m)
    (e : {i : Fin r // g i = a} ≃ Fin q) (B : Matrix (Fin q) (Fin t) ℝ)
    {i : Fin r} (hi : g i = a) (j : Fin t) :
    cavityGroupLift g a e B i j = B (e ⟨i, hi⟩) j := by
  simp only [cavityGroupLift, hi, dite_true]
```
Also tag the existing `cavityGroupLift_support` as `@[simp]`, or rename it to `cavityGroupLift_apply_of_ne` and make `hi` implicit-friendly. Then rewrite the proofs at lines 36/39, 48/49 and 88–99 as, for example, `simp only [cavityGroupLift_apply_of_eq _ _ _ _ hk]` and `simp [cavityGroupLift_support _ _ _ _ _ hk]`. The simp lemmas would discharge `hi` from the local context. Neither lemma can loop: in both, the right-hand side no longer contains `cavityGroupLift`.
findings.benefit: This gives one canonical normal form for entries of `cavityGroupLift`: `B (e ⟨i, hi⟩) j` on the group and `0` off it. That form does not depend on how the definition is written. The four proofs in this file become shorter and stop reaching into the definition body. Any later user evaluating lifted entries can use `simp [hi]` without unfolding. This also follows the convention used by sibling files in the same directory, which provide `@[simp] ..._apply` lemmas for their local matrix and map definitions.
